headline: Bitcoin is near $61,400 ahead of about $7.6 billion of bitcoin and ether options expiring at 08:00 UTC today (3pm Bangkok), while US bitcoin funds are on course for their worst month on record and sentiment sits at "Extreme Fear".

market.asOf: Read from CoinMarketCap at about 03:58 UTC Fri 27 Nov (10:58 Bangkok). The 24-hour changes for ETH and SOL are left out; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 11 out of 100 on both Alternative.me's index ("Extreme Fear", 13 a day earlier) and CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index. Read about 03:56-03:58 UTC Fri 27 Nov.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds head for their worst month since they launched
stories.summary: Money left US spot bitcoin funds for seven trading days in a row through Wednesday, and November's withdrawals have already passed the previous monthly record. US markets were shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday and stocks close early at 1pm ET on Friday.
points: US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $453.1 million on Wed 25 Nov, the seventh straight day of outflows; BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $329.7 million, per The Block.
November outflows total about $5.39 billion so far, already past the previous monthly record, per The Block.
Since 4 Oct the funds have shed 71,339 BTC (about $4.95 billion), with outflows on 22 of 35 trading days; they now hold about 1.24 million BTC, per Galaxy data cited by The Block.
US spot ether funds lost $68.5 million on Wednesday, their ninth straight outflow day, and about $1.3 billion so far in November, per The Block.

stories.title: About $7.6 billion of bitcoin and ether options expire at 08:00 UTC today, with most big bets on further falls
stories.summary: Bitcoin kept most of its bounce from Wednesday's low while US stock markets were closed, and traders betting on a fall took most of the forced selling. The biggest bets for Friday's options expiry are protection against further drops.
points: On Bitstamp, bitcoin fell to $57,209 on Wednesday and reached $61,509 on Thursday, per Bitcoin.com News; liquidations across the crypto market were under $313 million, and 75% ($237 million) were bets on a fall, per CoinGlass data it cites.

About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire on Deribit at 08:00 UTC on Friday 27 Nov (3:00am ET, 3:00pm Bangkok). CoinDesk puts the put/call ratio for that expiry at 0.89; Bitcoinist gives 0.85, $6.92 billion of bitcoin options and a "max pain" level of $71,000.
Deribit's volatility index (DVOL), a gauge of how big a move traders are pricing in, was 55.45, up from 38 at October's expiry, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Wall Street is split on the bitcoin bottom: JPMorgan sees 'capitulation', Galaxy withdraws its call that the bear market is over
stories.summary: JPMorgan analysts read Strategy (MSTR) trading below the value of its bitcoin as capitulation (sellers giving up). On the same day Galaxy's Alex Thorn withdrew Galaxy's October call that bitcoin's bear market ended in June, saying it is "very likely not over." These are analysts' readings, not forecasts.
points: Strategy's mNAV, its market value divided by the value of its bitcoin, fell to about 0.88x on Strategy's own dashboard, then recovered to 0.94x; JPMorgan called it a record low, per The Block.
JPMorgan puts bitcoin's production cost at about $86,000, which could pressure higher-cost miners while bitcoin trades near $60,000, per The Block.
Galaxy is watching a daily close below $58,525 (the 30 June closing low) and a $59,517 weekly close, per The Block.

briefs.title: Hong Kong market maker Auros to wind down
briefs.summary: Auros, a firm that keeps trading flowing on exchanges, is reportedly winding down after seven years; it traded more than $1.3 trillion in 2025, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: BitMart reported $319.5 million short
briefs.summary: Citing Nikkei Asia, Cointelegraph reports BitMart has a $319.5 million shortfall and $1.9 million of liquid assets for customer repayments, with Alvarez & Marsal overseeing the restructuring.

briefs.title: Zodia Custody breach confirmed
briefs.summary: Reuters reports an unauthorised party accessed limited client data at the Standard Chartered-backed custodian; Zodia says there were no unauthorised transactions.

briefs.title: KuCoin to delist Monero
briefs.summary: KuCoin removes its four XMR pairs at 08:00 UTC on 30 Nov; withdrawals stay open until 31 Dec. XMR fell almost 15%, to as low as $436, per U.Today.

briefs.title: US moves to recover Binance hack funds
briefs.summary: The Justice Department filed a civil lawsuit to recover more than $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency stolen in the October Binance hack, targeting USDC; over $2.9 billion of the more than $6 billion taken has been frozen, seized or returned, per GovInfoSecurity.

briefs.title: Senators push SEC to drop crypto exemption plan
briefs.summary: Senators Warren, Van Hollen, Smith and Reed asked SEC Chair Atkins to withdraw "Regulation Crypto Assets", which includes a $5 million startup exemption and a $75 million fundraising exemption, per The Block.

briefs.title: Fidelity files for a Chainlink fund
briefs.summary: Fidelity filed for a spot Chainlink ETF to trade on Nasdaq as FLNK, without staking, per The Block.

briefs.title: US Justice Department's biggest crypto scam crackdown
briefs.summary: The department targeted more than 800 defendants and froze more than $1 billion of stolen crypto, per The Block.

calendar.event: Deribit monthly bitcoin and ether options expiry
calendar.note: Settles at 08:00 UTC. About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire, put/call ratio 0.89, with large put bets at $60,000, $58,000, $50,000 and $40,000, per CoinDesk. Bitcoinist gives $6.92 billion, a put/call ratio of 0.85 and a "max pain" level of $71,000.

calendar.event: US stock markets close early after Thanksgiving
calendar.note: Stocks close at 1:00pm ET, per NYSE; SIFMA recommends a 2:00pm ET early close for US bond markets.

calendar.event: Binance Blockchain Week, Bangkok; Fed quiet period begins
calendar.note: At the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, per Khaosod English. The Fed's pre-meeting blackout runs from Sat 28 Nov to Thu 10 Dec, per the Fed's blackout calendar.

calendar.note: PROS and GRASS on Saturday 28; FF and CARDS on Sunday 29; GRVT, KMNO and GUN on Monday 30 (one tracker gives GUN on the 29th); EIGEN and SUI on Tuesday 1 Dec; M, BTW, ENA, 2Z and Q on Wednesday 2 Dec (M's date is disputed: Tokenomist shows 12 Dec); STO on Thursday 3 Dec; MMT and LA on Friday 4 Dec. See the unlock table on this page for sizes and confidence. (Dates from this desk's unlock data.)
October was 55.3, per Trading Economics; FXStreet lists 56.7 expected. Release time per MetaTrader.

calendar.event: Trump Media (DJT) noteholders can demand repayment
calendar.note: Holders of its convertible notes can require the company to buy them back for cash; about $883.5 million is outstanding after a $100 million buyback, per Trump Media.

calendar.event: MSCI removes Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes
calendar.note: Takes effect after the close on 30 Nov. MSCI-linked funds hold about 13 million MSTR shares, about 3.1% of the total; JPMorgan estimated about $2.8 billion of selling, per Cointelegraph.

calendar.event: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov), job openings (JOLTS, Oct); Fed's Bowman testifies to the House
calendar.note: ISM: October was 55.5, per ISM (ActionForex gives 55.4); ActionForex expects 53.8. ISM and JOLTS are both due at 10:00am, per FinanceCalendar. JOLTS: September was about 7.5 million, per the BLS; no consensus published. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman appears at the House Financial Services "Oversight of Prudential Regulators" hearing at 10:00am, per the Fed's calendar. Marvell reports after the close.
October was +86,000, per ADP. Salesforce and Snowflake report after the close; both calls are at 5:00pm ET, per the companies.
October was 54.5, per InvestingLive; ActionForex expects 54.9. Time per FinanceCalendar. The last weekly jobless claims reading was 189,000, per StockAnalysis.

Forecasts differ: U.S. Bank cites a +101,000 consensus, Continuum Economics expects +95,000 and Trading Economics +82,000. October payrolls rose 165,000 with unemployment at 4.1%, per the BLS, which schedules the release for 8:30am ET. University of Michigan's preliminary December sentiment follows at 10:00am ET (November final: 51.5, per FinanceCalendar).

Markets expect a rate hike, not a cut: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point hike at 99.4% on 26 Nov, per Invezz on TradingView; Longbridge reported 97.4%. Press conference at 2:30pm ET, per the Fed's calendar.
